transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me a little bit about what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Doc. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I had a bit of a situation at work. I'm a personal care aide, and we were having this staff meeting, and I just got really worked up. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room, dragging the chairs around and waving my arms to show everyone the proper angles for a catch, and I just couldn't seem to stop even when folks kept telling me to sit down. 

But honestly, those chairs they have in our breakroom are a hazard anyway. They have these little metal caps on the legs that scrape the linoleum right up. I was telling my buddy Frank about it—he drives a tow truck, completely different line of work, but he knows a ton about friction and weight distribution. We were down at the diner on 4th street talking about it last weekend. The one that serves breakfast all day? They have the best hashbrowns in the city, really crispy on the edges. I always tell the waitress to leave them on the grill an extra minute, it makes a huge difference. But yeah, anyway, my supervisor said I needed to come see someone after that meeting.
When you were explaining the chair issue to your supervisor, did you feel like there were hidden messages in the situation, or did you feel like you were seeing or hearing things that others weren't?

Hidden messages? No, no, my supervisor is pretty straightforward. I mean, she has terrible taste in scarves, always wearing these loud paisley things, but she says what she means. 

But about hearing things... well, yeah, I guess I do sometimes. Not at the meeting, but like, if I'm alone in the hallway at work, or at home down by the laundry room, I'll hear my name. Or I'll hear one of the residents calling out for help, clear as day. I always drop what I'm doing to go check, because you can't ignore a fall risk, but... there isn't anybody there. 

It happens a lot by my laundry room at home. I've got this old Maytag washer, the kind where the lint trap is actually on the top of the machine instead of inside the door? You can't even find parts for those anymore. I had to drive to three different hardware stores last month just to find a replacement knob for the timer. The kid working at the counter didn't even know what a Maytag was. He just kept looking at his phone. It's like nobody wants to learn how things actually work anymore, you know? They just want to buy a new one. I think it's a waste of money. But yeah... I'll hear my name or a resident calling, and the hallway is just totally empty.
Have you noticed any periods in your life where your mood was unusually high or low for days or weeks at a time, or where your energy levels were significantly different than usual?

Yeah, I guess there are times like that. Like, there are these stretches where I just feel so bright and fired up, you know? Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I have all this energy. I'll get so much done around the house. I actually reorganized my entire garage during one of those stretches. I built these custom shelves out of some scrap lumber I found behind the old bowling alley. You remember the one on 5th avenue? It closed down a few years ago. They had the best arcade games in the back. I used to spend hours playing Pac-Man there when I was a kid. The joystick on their machine was always a little sticky, though. Somebody probably spilled a soda on it. I hate when people don't clean up their messes. It's just disrespectful. 

But anyway, yeah, I get really fired up, but then... if someone slows me down or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. Like, way harder than I mean to. My sister came over while I was building those shelves and asked why I was doing it at 3 AM, and I just bit her head off. I felt bad about it later, but in the moment, I just couldn't stand being interrupted. I was on a roll, you know? I had my tape measure out, and my level... I bought this laser level recently, it's supposed to be perfectly accurate up to 50 feet. It's got this little red line that projects onto the wall. Really neat piece of technology. I got it on sale, too. But yeah, my mood definitely goes way up like that sometimes.
Do you find that you hear these voices even when you are feeling normal, or do they only happen when you are feeling that 'fired up' energy?

Well, no, it's not just when I'm all fired up. I mean, there was this one stretch not too long ago where I was actually feeling pretty calm. I was sleeping regular hours again, not running around building shelves or anything like that. I was just taking it easy, watching a lot of TV. Mostly those old westerns, you know? The ones in black and white. My dad used to love those. He had this big collection on VHS tapes, taking up a whole wall in the den. I don't even know if you can buy a VCR anymore, honestly. Probably have to go to a thrift store or something. I went to the Goodwill over on Elm Street last week looking for some work shirts, and they had a whole shelf of old electronics. Some of it was just junk, but they had this old ham radio that looked pretty cool. I almost bought it, but I don't have the space. 

But anyway, yeah, even during that calm stretch—which lasted for a few weeks, I think—I was still hearing it. I'd be sitting there watching TV, and I'd hear my name being called out, or a resident asking for help, clear as day. And honestly, during that same time, I was also pretty sure the people at work were keeping notes on me. Like, secret files or something. I kept catching them looking at me funny when I'd walk into the breakroom. Especially the new girl, Sarah. She's always carrying around this little spiral notebook. It's one of those ones with the college-ruled paper. I prefer wide-ruled myself, my handwriting is a little messy. But yeah, she was always scribbling in it, and I just knew it was about me. So yeah, the voices and the note-taking thing, that was happening even when I was feeling totally normal and sleeping fine.

During that calm period when you weren't feeling 'fired up' or unusually energetic, how long did those experiences—the voices and the feeling that your coworkers were keeping notes on you—continue for?

Well, like I said, it was a few weeks. Several weeks, really, where I was just feeling pretty normal, sleeping fine, not rushing around building shelves or anything. But the whole time, yeah, I was still hearing my name and I was just so sure about Sarah and her little notebook. It's funny, though, thinking about time like that. Weeks can feel so long when you're just sitting around watching TV. Have you ever noticed how the commercials on those old western channels are always for, like, reverse mortgages or life insurance? It's kind of depressing. I mean, I know their audience is mostly older folks, but still. It makes you think about getting older. My uncle got a reverse mortgage a few years back, and it turned into this huge mess with the bank. He lived in this beautiful old Victorian house with this wrap-around porch. You don't see porches like that much anymore. People just build these little concrete patios now. It's a shame. But anyway, yeah, the voices and the notebook thing... that went on for several weeks while I was otherwise feeling completely fine.
